To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the thyroid infiltrate in the high responder rat strains consists of a mixture of Ia+ macrophages and Ia- cytotoxic/supressor T cells, and that the degree of thyroid infiltration is related to the RT-1-MHC haplotypes.

the thyroid infiltrate in the Tg/CFA model of autoimmune thyroiditis is predominantly macrophages and cytotoxic/supressor T lymphocytes, that the degree of thyroiditis is related to the RT1-MHC haplotypes, and that thyroid epithelial Ia expression is not prominent.
the severity of thyroiditis induced in rats by thyroglobulin is strongly dependent upon both the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and the strain of the rat.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the mechanisms involved in the development of thyroiditis and the role played by the MHC.
the cellular and molecular events that lead to the development of thyroid autoimmunity and the mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of thyroid disease.
the study of thyroid autoimmunity in the rat.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thyroid is a privileged site for immune reactions, and that thyroiditis is a T cell-mediated disease, the severity of which is dependent on both the MHC and the antigen.

The main takeaway from our work is that
thyroiditis in the Lewis rat is a complex disease with both genetic and environmental components.
the cellular infiltrate in the thyroids of high responder rats is predominantly of the T lymphocyte and macrophage type and that this is related to the RT1-MHC haplotypes.
the cellular infiltrate in Tg-induced thyroiditis in the rat is dominated by macrophages, and that Tg-dependent thyroiditis in rats is strongly MHC restricted.
